title: Detection of isomorphisms at the point
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $q=p^a$ and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Let $n\ge1$, put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, and choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Use the bounded constructible point category $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], on the small pro-etale site of $s$: at integral coefficients this is the derived-complete category, at $E$ the rationalized category, and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ the common finite-stage category specified there. Let $\Lambda_s$ be its coefficient unit, with the stage-specific meaning of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] (the constant finite coefficient sheaf, the completed integral coefficient sheaf, or its rationalized/common-stage image), placed in cohomological degree zero. For every $P,Q\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ and every morphism $u:P\to Q$, $u$ is an isomorphism if and only if for every $r\in\mathbf Z$ the postcomposition map
$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_c(s,\Lambda)}(\Lambda_s[-r],P)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_c(s,\Lambda)}(\Lambda_s[-r],Q),\qquad g\longmapsto u\circ g,
$$
is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-modules (equivalently, is bijective).

proof.text: If $u$ is invertible, postcomposition with $u^{-1}$ is inverse to postcomposition with $u$ on $\operatorname{Hom}_s(\Lambda[-r],-)$: $(u^{-1}\circ u)\circ g=g$ and $(u\circ u^{-1})\circ h=h$. This proves the forward implication for every integer $r$, at every coefficient stage.

source.place: Proof, implication from an isomorphism to isomorphisms on all cohomology modules

proof.text: Conversely assume all the displayed Hom maps are isomorphisms. Write $F=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ and $v=F(u)$. Use the four actual targets of $F$ in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]: $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$, and the common-stage category $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$. Each $F$ is an exact equivalence by [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence]. Use only the last, cohomological identity in [lem-sf-point], interpreted with these coefficient-specific targets. Its natural identifications $\theta^r_C:\operatorname{Hom}_s(\Lambda[-r],C)\simeq H^r(F(C))$ give $H^r(v)\theta^r_P=\theta^r_Q\operatorname{Hom}_s(\Lambda[-r],u)$. Thus each $H^r(v)$ is invertible. Use the cohomology functors and their action on morphisms from [def-weil-coefficient-cohomology-modules]. At $\Qlb$, this means the map on the cohomology vector spaces obtained by scalar extension to $\Qlb$ from a common finite field of definition is bijective. The target $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$ printed in [lem-sf-point] is used only at finite coefficients; its unqualified use at the other stages is a source error, not an identification used here.

source.place: The three displayed point equivalences and the final stagewise equivalence; item proof, cohomology/Hom identification

proof.text: For $\Lambda=A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E$, or $E$, regard $v$ in the ordinary derived category of $\Lambda$-modules. These target categories are full subcategories, as specified in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] with $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda$: the cohomology maps from step 2 make $v$ invertible in $D(\Lambda)$. Its inverse is a morphism between the same two objects and hence lies in the full subcategory. Finally the equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] reflects this inverse: lift it by fullness to $w:Q\to P$; faithfulness applied to $F(wu)=1$ and $F(uw)=1$ gives $wu=1$ and $uw=1$. Thus $u$ is invertible at these three stages.

source.place: Tag 05RT, label lemma-acyclic; cohomological criterion also in Mathlib DerivedCategory.isIso_iff, HomologySequence.lean:88-89

proof.text: For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, use [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category], rather than identifying that category with an ambient category of arbitrary sheaves or arbitrary $\Qlb$-complexes. The two objects and $v$ have a representative $v_L:V\to W$ in $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(L)$ over a common finite extension $L/\Ql$. By the definition of cohomology at the algebraically closed stage in [def-weil-coefficient-cohomology-modules], together with the scalar-extension cohomology formula in the common-stage definition, step 2 says that $H^r(v_L)\otimes_L\Qlb$ is bijective for every $r$. In bases the matrix of $H^r(v_L)$ has entries in $L$; its rank is the largest size of a nonzero minor, and a minor is nonzero in $L$ exactly when it is nonzero in $\Qlb$. Hence its rank equals both source and target dimensions already over $L$, so $H^r(v_L)$ is bijective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] to $\operatorname{Mod}_L$ to invert $v_L$ in $D(L)$; the inverse belongs to the same full finite-dimensional bounded subcategory. Write $F(P)=(E_0,A)$, $F(Q)=(E_1,B)$ and $v=[L,v_L]$, so $V=T_{L/E_0}A$ and $W=T_{L/E_1}B$. The class $[L,v_L^{-1}]$ is a morphism $F(Q)\to F(P)$. By the defining composition rule its composites with $v$ are $[L,\operatorname{id}_V]$ and $[L,\operatorname{id}_W]$. These are the identities of $F(P)$ and $F(Q)$: their identity representatives at $E_0$ and $E_1$ transition to $\operatorname{id}_V$ and $\operatorname{id}_W$ at $L$, since the transition is a functor conjugated by the tower isomorphisms. The equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] reflects this inverse by the fullness-and-faithfulness argument of step 3. This proves the converse also at the algebraically closed stage.

source.place: Final displayed equivalence and preceding definition of the common finite-stage colimit; item proof, reduction to module complexes

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q33-73f15c22c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery and changed nothing. It is the item plus its report: no new nodes, no fixes, no SGA citation. Statement: the claim of blueprint lem-sf-detection (master order 2183, main-20261015 order 2527) is kept exactly. Its 'In the setting of' is replaced by the explicit datum: four coefficient stages, s = Spec k, the point category of def-weil-finite-coefficient-point, and Λ_s from def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology. Both implications, every shift r and arbitrary morphisms are kept; nothing is weakened. Source error: confirmed. lem-sf-point's unqualified target D^b_fin(A_{E,n}) is false at the stages O_E, E and Q̄_ℓ. End(Λ_s) = O_E has characteristic 0, while every endomorphism ring in D(A_{E,n}) is killed by ℓ^n, and any additive equivalence preserves endomorphism rings. The item uses only lem-sf-point's H^r = Hom_s(Λ[-r],-) clause, which is true at all four stages, together with lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence for the correct targets. Step 1 is elementary. Step 2 uses the naturality of that clause (an identity of functors) and the H^i functors of def-weil-coefficient-cohomology-modules, including the Q̄_ℓ-stage formula. Step 3 uses the Mathlib leaf DerivedCategory.isIso_iff (lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology) over Mod_Λ, the full-subcategory clauses of the targets, and reflection of the inverse by fullness and faithfulness. Step 4 I checked against the full definition of def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category: the rank of a matrix does not change under field extension, v_L is inverted at a common stage L, and the composites [L,id] are the transported identities. Edge cases I checked: zero objects, negative r, n = 1, integral torsion, zero-dimensional cohomology. Route: lem-sf-point's unit sk-thm-sf-global-duality is cited by the item's unit. sk-def-sf-admissible is also reached transitively, so the declared tool_use is harmless and I accept it. Duplicate search with rg over snapshot/dag/nodes found none. Leaving out the étale Lean attachment is correct. Minor point: at the Q̄_ℓ stage the Hom sets are only defined as colimits of abelian groups, so 'isomorphism of Λ-modules' rests on the parenthetical 'equivalently bijective'; acceptable as written. Note for the owner of thm-sf-identification: its step 3 concludes that two maps are equal from this lemma, which only detects isomorphisms. Details are in review.md.
